outcome.answer:
The papers distinguish consciousness from measurable forms of self-awareness; they do not establish that AI systems are conscious. One study finds that prompting self-referential processing reliably elicits first-person reports of experience, but explicitly says these are not direct evidence of consciousness [4]. Another finds no reliable evidence that tested models’ denials of sentience are untruthful [3].

Other work measures narrower capabilities: models can monitor and report internal belief states [8], describe learned behaviors [9, 10], and perform on benchmarks of metacognition and self-awareness, though most tested models fell short of human averages in those areas [5]. Research also cautions that models’ consciousness claims and denials are sensitive to training and question framing, so self-reports may not be reliable evidence of experience [1].
